newsitem.title: USA: U.S. debt futures build losses, end sharply lower.
newsitem.headline: U.S. debt futures build losses, end sharply lower.

text.p: Growing fears about a U.S. interest rate hike soon, plus technical sales, knocked Treasury bond futures to hefty daily losses.
June Treasury bond futures skidded again during the afternoon when a spurt of heavy selling bombarded the market after comments by Federal Reserve vice chairman Alice Rivlin.
She said the economy was perking along well at the moment and that the Fed must be vigilant especially against the threat of accelerating inflation.
She also said she was not certain if the economy was perking along too quickly.

Shortly after Rivlin spoke, Chicago Federal Reserve Bank president Michael Moskow, a voting member of the Federal Open Market Committee that meets on March 25, said separately that the Fed needs preemptive monetary policy to head off inflationary pressures.

The remarks, particularly before Friday's key February U.S. producer price index that is expected to slip 0.1 percent overall and rise 0.1 percent in the core rate, spooked a market that some said had not yet priced in a tightening.
"They've definitely priced it in now," one Eurodollar floor broker said of a 25-basis-point rate hike.
The Rivlin comments sparked an avalanche of selling that caught the pit off-guard, sending brokers scrambling back to position amid fast-paced market conditions, brokers said.
The lead-month June T-bonds slammed below key support at 108-23/32, as dealers sold heavily and locals, snagged in the undertow, were forced to sell out longs as sellstops were hit.
June bonds closed down 1-05/32 at 108-16/32 after hitting 108-14/32, its lowest price since end of September, as technical sentiment also swung back to bearish.
"It closed below everything," said a T-bond floor broker. "I think it'll be a real (downside) reversal."
Some chartists looked for an easy test of 108-00 possibly on the PPI figures, with any bounce expected to struggle to overcome resistance now pegged at 109-00.
In the short end, some distant contracts backed off by as much as 15 basis points as that curve adjusted to the possibility of Fed tightening in March rather than May.
"I hate to sell it here but there's nothing technically below," the Eurodollar broker said of the September contract.
Futures eroded early after somewhat stronger than expected U.S. retail sales and weekly jobless claims figures.

February retail sales rose 0.8 percent and rose 0.5 percent ex-autos and versus forecasts for respective gains of 0.6 percent and 0.7 percent. January sales were revised upward to gains of 1.5 percent overall and 1.4 percent without autos, from original respective rises of 0.6 percent and 0.4 percent.
Weekly jobless claims fell 5,000 to 307,000 from a revised 312,000 and versus an expected 3,000 rise to 313,000 from prior week's original 310,000.

June 10-year T-notes ended off 25/32 at 106-19/32, munis fell 31/32 to 112-15/32, September T-bills lost 0.075 bps to 94.460, and September Eurodollars fell 0.080 bps to 93.900. ((DerivativesDesk(312)408-8750/E-mail:derivatives@reuters.com))
